unresolved.observation: Thin rear-middle horizontal chain crosses the thick nearer-right top marker/vertical region. No independent marker contour, center or fill class can be resolved for the nominal rear-middle-center slot.
unresolved.prohibitedInference: Do not assert a hidden visible particle, its species, exact center, radius or unbroken hidden connector geometry from these pixels.

connectorChains.meaning: Each list gives the ordered apparent endpoints along a three-slot chain. Adjacent endpoints are connected by visible strokes except where foreground occlusion or dash breaks intervene. A list through R-C-M-slot is an unresolved chain, not proof of a separately visible point. The 27 chains imply 54 nominal adjacent relationships but not 54 wholly visible segments.

lineAppearance: Nearer front-plane lines are heavy and solid. More distant horizontal and vertical lines are generally thinner.
Depth chains rise to the right from nearer to rear apparent planes. Across chains slope gently downward to the right; vertical chains are approximately vertical.

Rear-left vertical chain R-L-T to R-L-M to R-L-B contains clear dash/gap interruptions, including between the upper intermediate horizontal stroke and R-L-M and below R-L-M. It is not a continuous heavy foreground line.

Rear-bottom across chain is thin with visible interruptions near foreground crossings and the intermediate-right vertical. Some gaps are occlusion rather than evidence of a uniformly repeated dash pattern.
Other thin rear strokes also disappear under thicker foreground markers/lines. Do not classify every missing fragment as a dashed edge or invent extra junctions at projected crossings.
Visible connectors generally stop at or merge into marker rims; they do not pass through open white disk interiors. Highlights and short rim accents are marker appearance, not extra points.
geometry: Two nearest-neighbor steps along each of three apparent directions form the finite framework. Filled and open markers alternate at distinguishable adjacent sites.
Apparent marker size decreases from nearer to rear planes. Across spacing and vertical lengths also vary with apparent plane.
The drawing is rough/perspectival, not an exact equal-step affine projection. There are no axis arrows, ticks, coordinates, units, dimensions or numeric distances.
No Euclidean angle, physical length, charge, ion radius, chemical formula or measured 3D calibration is supplied in the pixels.
There are no visible alphabetic labels, legend, caption, flags, cultural symbols, people, apparatus or additional subfigures inside this PNG.
instructionalContextOnly: The source-only lesson associates fig-11 with table salt and describes connecting equilibrium-position centers into a spatial crystal lattice. This context does not resolve occluded source pixels or give quantitative physical calibration.
uncertainties: The unresolved rear-middle-center slot must remain distinct from the 26 actually distinguishable markers.
Some dark disks have white highlights or slivers but still read as filled, not as additional open-marker classes.
Exact raster centers, radii, tangent endpoints and line widths are approximate because of scan jaggedness and overlap.
Depth shading/line weight and selective gaps establish occlusion; not every hidden continuation or dash schedule is observable.
A complete ideal 27-particle cube, species assignment and physical metric must not be treated as source facts.
